title: Game Center, iOS 4.1, 2010
lede: Apple’s social gaming app, dressed as a casino card table of green felt framed in wood.
summary: Green felt, a wooden table rim, and game chips. Apple, 2010.

evidence.note: No image of 800 px or more was found under a usable source. Based on Wikipedia and Fast Company (2012).

styles.note: A clear object metaphor: a card table with felt cloth and chips, pushed by Steve Jobs according to former Apple designers.

context: Game Center was released to the public on 8 September 2010 with iOS 4.1. Its developer preview “had a dark appearance with abstract colors”; the release changed to “a lighter ‘game board’ appearance with more skeuomorphic design elements.” [Wikipedia: Game Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_Center).

A former Apple designer told Fast Company: “Steve pushed very hard to have everything—the felt-cloth table, the game chips—look like they would in real life.” [Fast Company, Austin Carr, “Will Apple’s Tacky Software-Design Philosophy Cause A Revolt?” (2012)](https://www.fastcompany.com/1670760/will-apples-tacky-software-design-philosophy-cause-a-revolt).
interpretation: The shift from an abstract dark preview to felt and wood at release shows the style as a deliberate late choice, not a default.
next: Find a large screenshot of the iOS 4–6 Game Center and inspect the felt and wood textures.
